newsitem.title: CHILE: CTC price already reflects VTR deal -- Santander.
newsitem.headline: CTC price already reflects VTR deal -- Santander.

text.p: Share price rises by Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile (CTC) in recent weeks show that the market has factored in its expected merger with long-distance competitor VTR, Santander Investment said.
Santander, in its weekly equities bulletin, recommended waiting until the VTR negotiation pans out before taking a long-term position on CTC's stock.

"We recommend waiting until the whole process of negotiation with VTR is finished, and its conditions and characteristics are formally announced, before again taking a long-term position on CTC," it said.

CTC, owned about 43 percent by Telefonica de Espana, and VTR, owned by Chile's Luksic group and Southwestern Bell, have been in merger talks for weeks in a process that has shaken up Chile's ultra-competitive telecom industry.
Local news reports say negotiations have hit snags on how much money will change hands and on the terms for SBC's withdrawal from VTR.
CTC's local shares were up 3.78 percent at 3,710 pesos Wednesday, up from a year low of 2,150 pesos.

Santander also said it expected Peruvian utility Egenor's share price on the Lima stock exchange to rise above the price paid by Chilgener this month, when it bought 29 percent of Egenor for $123 million.
The recently-privatized Egenor began trading on the Lima exchange this month and closed at 1.70 soles on Wednesday.
